01 — Orientation

What this site is

Majesty Tours' site is a static website — plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no server-side application and no database behind it. A small content-editing tool sits on top so someone non-technical can update prices, tour text and photos without touching code.

The website

What visitors see — journeys, gallery, fleet, contact form. Plain static pages.

The admin area

A content editor at /admin ("Decap CMS") for the two files that drive the site's text and photos.

Netlify

Hosts the site and rebuilds it automatically the moment content changes.

Google Sheets

Where inquiry-form and partner-registration submissions actually land.

There are no customer accounts anywhere on the public site — visitors never create a password. The only login on the entire site is the admin login used to edit content.

02 — The public experience

Visiting the site

One long scrolling homepage with a sticky nav — Journeys, Day Trips, The Island, When to go, Gallery, Fleet — plus a Plan a journey button that jumps straight to the contact form.

Homepage

Journeys (tours)

Each of the 7 signature tours is listed with its route, price and duration. The + button adds a tour to the visitor's inquiry selection (more on that below); clicking the tour's name expands its full day-by-day itinerary, photos and highlights inline.

Planning a journey (the "selection", not a shopping cart)

There's no payment or checkout on this site. The + buttons build a simple shortlist a visitor can send along with their inquiry:

  1. Visitor clicks + on any journey or add-on, anywhere on the page.
  2. It appears in the "Your selection" panel inside the contact form, and in a small floating bubble in the corner of the screen.
  3. They fill in name, phone and email and submit — their selection travels with the message.

This selection lives only in the visitor's own browser until the moment they submit — see Where data lives.

Footer, legal pages & partner registration

The footer links to Privacy, Terms, Cancellation Policy, and Partner Registration, plus the review-platform and social links managed in the CMS.

03 — The part most guides skip

Where your data actually lives

In plain terms: there is no traditional database behind this site. The site's own text and photos live as two plain files that a save in the admin tool updates directly; everything a visitor submits goes straight to Google Sheets instead.

A visitor's selection ("cart")their own browser—Cleared if they clear browsing data; never sent until they submit

The selection / cart, specifically

It's intentionally lightweight: it lives only in that one visitor's browser for as long as they keep it, and is bundled into the inquiry only at the moment they submit the contact form. It never touches a server before that.

04 — Running the content

Admin guide

Logging in

The content editor lives at:

https://<your-site-domain>/admin/

It's built on Decap CMS and protected by Netlify Identity — the same sign-in system Netlify uses for its own dashboard. New admins are invited from Netlify dashboard → Identity tab on the site's Netlify project — never from anywhere on the website itself.

Illustrative — placeholders only

On the real site, that click opens a popup asking for your email and password, shown below with placeholder values only — never real credentials.

Netlify Identity
Sign in
you@example.com
••••••••
Log in

Forgotten your password? Use "Forgot password" inside that same popup — it emails a reset link to the address your account was invited with.

The Content screen

Once signed in, you land on Contents, with one collection, Website Content, holding two entries:

Contact & Info

Top to bottom: Contact Details, Platform Links (Google/TripAdvisor/Airbnb/GetYourGuide/Viator/TourRadar), Social Media Links (Instagram/Facebook/TikTok), Stats (years guiding, routes mapped, traveller rating), and finally Tours.

Tours — what you can and can't change

Guardrail

You cannot add, remove, or reorder tours (or their slideshow photos) here. Each tour and each slide maps to a fixed, hand-built block of HTML on the live page by its position in the list — a new slot wouldn't create a matching spot on the site, and removing one would leave a broken slide behind.

Reordering slideshow photos within a tour is safe. Every other field in a tour — name, price, overview, itinerary, highlights, inclusions, themes, facts — is safe to edit freely.

Gallery Photos

Unlike Tours, this list is fully open — add or remove as many entries as you like. Each item is either:

  • a photo — set Photo, leave Video/Poster blank, or
  • a video — set Video (an .mp4) and Video Poster (its thumbnail), leave Photo blank.

Every item needs a Caption.

Uploading photos & videos

Clicking any image or file field — Photo, Video Poster, a slideshow image — opens the Media Library: the assets/ folder as a searchable grid. Upload adds a new file from your computer; existing files can be reused across any field on the site.

Saving & publishing

Decap CMS auto-saves your in-progress edits as a draft while you type. When you're done, use Publish to commit the change — that's the point it actually goes live (see how an edit reaches the site). Give it a minute or two afterwards before checking the live page.

05 — Leads & applications

Where form submissions go

Neither of the site's two forms is stored in the CMS or anywhere on the website — both post straight to Google Sheets through a Google Apps Script link.

"Plan a journey" inquiries

Homepage contact form → its own Google Sheet, one row per inquiry, selection included.

Partner registrations

register.html → a separate Google Sheet, one row per applicant, with their generated Partner ID.

If you need access to either sheet, ask whoever set up the Google Apps Script integration for edit access — the CMS login doesn't grant it.

06 — Common questions

FAQ

I edited a tour's price in the CMS but the cart still shows the old price — is that a bug?
No — this used to happen but was fixed. As long as you save and publish the edit, the selection panel and inquiry form now stay in sync with whatever the CMS shows.
Can I reorder the tours themselves?
No — reordering, adding, or removing tours isn't possible from the CMS, because each one is tied to a specific hand-built block on the page. That needs a code change from your developer.
Where do I see who filled out the contact form or applied as a partner?
In Google Sheets, not on the website — see Where form submissions go.
I forgot my admin password.
Use "Forgot password" on the Netlify Identity popup at /admin/. If you don't have an account yet, someone with access to the Netlify project's Identity tab needs to invite you.
Do visitors ever create an account or log in?
No. Browsing, the journey selection, and the inquiry/registration forms are all account-free. The only login on the entire site is the admin one described above.
